D26 — 2026-10-04
chose: Stop's git question (D11, D23) is scoped and cached, and the gate stays on. (1) Scope: `git status … -- <pathspecs>`. The pathspecs are every positive guard glob and file mention of an in-force rule, as `:(glob)**/<tail>` because a guard matches by tail. Any pattern git's glob cannot match as a guard does (`[`, `]`, `\`, `:`, a leading `/`, a `**` inside a segment) falls back to the whole tree. (2) Cache: the session's write mark counts may-write commands. Stop keeps git's answer under that count and a key of the pathspec set, and asks again only after another may-write command or a change in the rules' scope. A git failure is never cached.
over: Defaulting the gate off (R4-A carries round 4's main claim, D9). An in-process walk or a .git/index parse instead of the spawn (tail globs force a whole-tree walk, plus a binary index reader mirrored in Rust).
because: The orchestrator asked for marked-session Stop to be cut before A and C. Measured on i1000 as a real git repo, interleaved against rc.4, the same written-back session:
- Before: +32.2 ms (+46.9%).
- After, repeated Stops: TS +2.3 ms (+3.4%), Rust core −15.2 ms (−22.7%).
- After, the first Stop after a new write (cache miss each time): TS +32.4 ms, Rust +20.1 ms.
